{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-al-d","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"c8957050fee7f1a0be5398594775306e89b959dbe50b946487f064549dd688ea","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-al-class-d:lineage:5","source_registry_sha256":"ea8231e949706ecda9f2a398d6eaf9ab30e224ac7defb0e6291b764b84ed0d95","source_liveness_sha256":"e524456f547beacfeca0647b02ef401523e58aa5b835501e7cbdd821b6546315"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Testing, renewal and license classes","heading":"C — Testing, renewal and license classes","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Testing, renewal and license classes

FACT_ID: sec02-F01 | anchor: A13
A driver restricted to corrective lenses must wear them during the road test. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-F02 | anchor: A13
If the vision exam shows you need lenses to see better, you will be required to wear corrective lenses whenever you drive. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-F03 | anchor: A13
Failing the vision exam means seeing a licensed eye specialist and returning the report to the examiner; if it shows you see well enough to drive safely, you may finish the test. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-F04 | anchor: A13
The knowledge test asks about Alabama traffic laws, road signs and safe-driving rules, and its questions come from this manual. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-F05 | anchor: A13
A learner-license applicant receives the learner license after passing the knowledge test and paying the fee, while a regular-license applicant receives the license after passing the road test and paying the fee. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-F06 | anchor: A13
Someone applying for both a motor driven cycle license and a learner license must take both exams, and cycle or motorcycle applicants study the separate motorcycle manual. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-F07 | anchor: A13
Automated testing is offered to every applicant who takes the knowledge test. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-F08 | anchor: A13
The road test, given by a driver license examiner, is the last step toward driving on public roads, and a 16-year-old applicant must come with a parent or guardian. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-F09 | anchor: A13
Before the road test the examiner checks that the vehicle is safe and has brake lights, left and right turn signals, and a horn. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-F10 | anchor: A13
You must show proof of insurance and registration for the road test, and a rental car qualifies only if you are named on the rental agreement as an additional driver. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-F11 | anchor: A14
Check tire pressure monthly with a gauge while the tires are cold, matching the reading to the PSI number on the door-jamb sticker by adding or releasing air. [A14]
Source: [A14 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-F12 | anchor: A14
For the penny tread test, insert Lincoln's head first into the deepest groove; if his whole head shows, the tires are too worn to drive on and need replacing. [A14]
Source: [A14 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-F13 | anchor: A14
Sit upright with your back against the seat and feet on the floor, because slouching can make the restraint system less effective. [A14]
Source: [A14 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-F14 | anchor: A14
Keep your heel on the floor while your foot pivots between brake and accelerator, and set the steering wheel top no higher than your shoulders and below your chin. [A14]
Source: [A14 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-F15 | anchor: A14
A driver who seems to have an impairment affecting driving may need a physician's statement and periodic examiner checks, and failing to report the condition can lead to revocation. [A14]
Source: [A14 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-F16 | anchor: A14
A non-driver ID card needs the same identity proof as a license and serves people who cannot physically qualify, hold no current Alabama license, or are giving up driving. [A14]
Source: [A14 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-F17 | anchor: A15
An Alabama license expires four years after issue and may be renewed any time within 180 days before the expiration date printed on it. [A15]
Source: [A15 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-F18 | anchor: A15
Military members and dependents, college students and others temporarily out of state for work may renew by mail if their photo-and-signature license was issued within the last four years. [A15]
Source: [A15 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-F19 | anchor: A15
State law gives a 60-day grace period after expiration for renewal, and the license stays valid during that period. [A15]
Source: [A15 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-F20 | anchor: A15
A license can be renewed without an exam within 3 years after expiring, and the new license runs four years from the last expiration date, not from the issue date. [A15]
Source: [A15 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-F21 | anchor: A15
Although renewal stays possible up to three years after expiration, you may not legally drive on an expired license. [A15]
Why it matters: a late-renewal window is not permission to drive; only the short grace period keeps the license valid.
Source: [A15 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-F22 | anchor: A15
An unexpired license that is lost, destroyed or unreadable is replaced with a duplicate from the Probate Judge or License Commissioner, with no exam but with proof of identity such as a certified birth certificate. [A15]
Source: [A15 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-F23 | anchor: A15
A false affidavit used to get a duplicate license can bring forgery or perjury charges, or both, punished by fine, prison or both. [A15]
Source: [A15 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-F24 | anchor: A15
Adding, changing or removing classes, restrictions or endorsements requires a driver license examiner, and licenses and ID cards are never forwarded to another address. [A15]
Source: [A15 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-F25 | anchor: A16
A name change needs documents such as a marriage certificate or court order with an updated Social Security card, and STAR ID holders must make it at an ALEA office. [A16]
Source: [A16 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec02-F26 | anchor: A16
After moving within Alabama you have 30 days to tell the Driver License Division your new address, which is updated on your record free of charge without reissuing the card. [A16]
Source: [A16 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec02-F27 | anchor: A16
Class D covers generally all passenger vehicles not in Classes A, B, C or M; Class M covers motorcycles and motor-driven cycles, and Class V covers motorized watercraft. [A16]
Source: [A16 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec02-F28 | anchor: A17
Class A is for combination vehicles with a combined weight rating over 26,000 pounds when the towed vehicle is rated over 10,000 pounds. [A17]
Source: [A17 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F29 | anchor: A17
Class B is for single vehicles rated over 26,000 pounds towing no more than 10,000 pounds, and Class C is for vehicles built for 16 or more people including the driver or placarded for hazardous materials. [A17]
Source: [A17 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F30 | anchor: A17
Higher classes include lower ones: Class A holders may drive Class B, C and D vehicles, Class B holders Class C and D, and Class C holders Class D. [A17]
Source: [A17 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F31 | anchor: A17
Anyone who turned 12 after January 1, 2002 and holds a vessel license may operate a vessel only with a licensed adult aged 21 or older aboard and ready to take control, though a licensed operator aged 14 or older may operate alone. [A17]
Source: [A17 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F32 | anchor: A17
People born before April 28, 1954 need no vessel exam but must still visit a driver license office to have the vessel class issued. [A17]
Source: [A17 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F33 | anchor: A18
While driving you must carry the proper license or learner permit and show it to any law enforcement officer who asks. [A18]
Source: [A18 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F34 | anchor: A18
Under the Hands-Free Law effective June 2024, holding a wireless device is a violation when the driver is seen drifting across lanes without signaling, swerving, or otherwise driving improperly. [A18]
Why it matters: the violation is tied to holding the device while driving improperly, not to merely having a phone in the car.
Source: [A18 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F35 | anchor: A18
Within a 24-month period, hands-free convictions cost a $50 fine and 1 point the first time, $100 and 2 points the second, and $150 and 3 points the third. [A18]
Source: [A18 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F36 | anchor: A18
For this law a wireless device means any device used to start or receive communication information or data. [A18]
Source: [A18 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0018]

Glossary: grace period — the short time after expiration when the license stays valid for renewal [A15]. Duplicate license — a replacement for an unexpired lost or unreadable license [A15]. Non-driver ID card — state identification for people who do not drive [A14].
Memory aid: hands-free penalties climb one step per conviction, with points rising one, two, three [A18].
